Fresh singleton and exhaustive subset BFS check for n=2..6
correctness.rationale: The distance-two condition suffices: on a geodesic minimizing selected internal vertices, replace any selected midpoint by an unselected common neighbor. The resulting walk is still a geodesic, since it has the same minimum length. Fibonacci-cube distances are Hamming distances by removing differing ones before inserting new ones. Thus a pair of neighbors of a given word has a unique midpoint exactly when their flips insert ones at two adjacent positions; a simultaneous deletion or mixed flip cannot introduce adjacent ones. This excludes the all-zero word for n>=2, leading/trailing zero runs of length at least three, and internal runs of at least four. Distance-two pairs with two midpoints give exactly the opposite-corner conflicts, so feasible sets are precisely the independent sets in the claimed graph. The length enumerator follows by multiplying the two end-run choices and summing over internal gaps. In the factorization (1+z)(1-z-z^3) the positive cubic root r is simple; the other cubic roots are a conjugate pair with modulus r^(-1/2)>1, so the next contribution is bounded. Greedy independence and maximum degree at most binom(n,2) preserve the exponential rate. A fresh exhaustive check for n=2 through 6 matched direct all-pairs visibility for every eligible subset and matched eligibility for every singleton, with maxima 2,3,5,5,9. Replay recipe: enumerate no-11 words, connect Hamming-distance-one words, and for each pair remove the selected vertices other than the endpoints and compare restricted and original BFS distances.
residual_risks: The finite check establishes no claims beyond its dimensions. The asymptotic conclusion is an nth-root limit, not a constant-factor equivalent for the optimum.

evidence: Cicerone et al. give a general bypass-vertex criterion for zero total mutual-visibility number; Bujtás–Klavžar–Tian give the square criterion in Hamming graphs. The accessible preprint conclusion is not assumed to reproduce the journal discussion of Fibonacci cubes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general criterion locates the type of local obstruction but does not supply the Fibonacci-word enumeration or a large independent set in its actual conflict graph. An isometric induced cube subgraph is not covered by treating it as a full Hamming graph.

evidence: The official text announces bounds using maximal Fibonacci strings and the daisy-cube representation, plus small exact values; it gives no asymptotic order. The frozen growth proof uses a complete eligibility count and upper and lower bounds differing by only a polynomial factor.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Bounds known to differ from the same exponential function by subexponential factors would imply the frozen rate even without stating the root. The available abstract does not give such quantitative bounds. A full Hamming square characterization and a general zero test do not give that implication.

evidence: Theorem 6 forbids selected distance-two pairs in full Hamming graphs. For a Fibonacci string, the zero-run eligibility rule also says that the vertices still insertable into its path independent set form an independent set. This is equivalent to a unique coordinatewise maximal Fibonacci superword: all insertable positions can be added together exactly in that case.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The maximal-string equivalence explains the strong relevance of the daisy-cube approach. The Hamming result alone cannot replace the conflict characterization: a missing square corner can already make a singleton infeasible.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct content is the explicit eligible-word and conflict characterization in Fibonacci cubes, its enumerator, and the resulting exact exponential growth rate. Hamming-graph square criteria and general singleton criteria are credited. The closest public same-family abstract announces results and a closely related method, but the exact available wording gives neither bounds nor a rate and supplies no demonstrable implication of the frozen result.
residual_risks: The mathematical details of Podrug–Bujtás–Klavžar–Tan could yield the same characterization or a matching or stronger exponential bound; no lawful full text was located. The journal-only comparison at DOI:10.1016/j.amc.2024.129216 remains limited.

value.rationale: The result replaces an all-pairs geodesic set optimization by explicit forbidden words and a sparse conflict graph for every dimension. It quantifies exponential separation between the eligible census and the unrestricted size of the Fibonacci cube and identifies the exponential growth of the actual visibility optimum. Those structural and asymptotic conclusions are materially more useful than a list of finite maxima.
residual_risks: No closed finite optimum or precise multiplicative asymptotics are given.
